text: 你每刷一次手机，都在给未来的自己挖坟。
en: Every time you scroll your phone, you are digging a grave for your future self.

text: 三年后，你会发现自己活在一个由算法亲手打造的活棺材里，连喊救命都只听见自己的回音。
en: Three years later, you will find yourself living in a living coffin hand-built by algorithms, where even crying for help only echoes back to yourself.

text: 公元前210年，秦始皇死在沙丘，赵高扣下遗诏，逼死扶苏，扶胡亥登基。
en: In 210 BC, Qin Shi Huang died at Shaqiu. Zhao Gao withheld the final edict, forced Fusu to death, and installed Hu Hai on the throne.

text: 从此，胡亥听到的每一句话，都经过赵高过滤。
en: From then on, every word Hu Hai heard had been filtered by Zhao Gao.

text: 赵高牵来一头鹿，当着满朝文武说：“这是马。
en: Zhao Gao led a deer before the full court and said: 'This is a horse.

text: ”胡亥笑了：“丞相错了，这是鹿。
en: ' Hu Hai laughed: 'Chancellor, you are wrong; this is a deer.

text: 他问左右，有人沉默，有人说是马，胡亥开始怀疑自己的眼睛，最后被赵高软禁，逼他自杀，他死前想吃一口粗粮，都没人给他。
en: He asked those around him: some were silent, some said it was a horse. Hu Hai began doubting his own eyes, and was finally placed under house arrest by Zhao Gao and forced to commit suicide. Before dying, he wanted a bite of coarse grain, and no one gave it to him.

text: 一个皇帝，被信息茧房活活饿死。
en: An emperor starved to death by an information cocoon.

text: 这不是古代专利。
en: This is not exclusive to ancient times.

text: 今天你手机里的算法，就是赵高。
en: Today, the algorithm in your phone is Zhao Gao.

text: 它知道你爱看什么，恨什么，怕什么。
en: It knows what you love to watch, hate, and fear.

text: 你点了一个“男人没一个好东西”，它给你推一百条“渣男实录”。
en: You click one 'no man is any good', and it pushes you a hundred 'scumbag chronicles'.

text: 你点了一个“穷人就是懒”，它给你推一千条“底层互害”，你以为你在看世界，其实是世界在看你的笑话。
en: You click one 'poor people are just lazy', and it pushes you a thousand 'bottom-level mutual harm' pieces. You think you are watching the world, but in fact the world is laughing at you.

text: 心理学上，这叫“确认偏误”。
en: In psychology, this is called 'confirmation bias'.

text: 你只相信你愿意相信的，大脑为了省能量，自动屏蔽反对声音。
en: You only believe what you are willing to believe; to save energy, the brain automatically blocks opposing voices.

text: 算法把这套本能放大了一万倍，再加上“回音室效应”，你身边全是和你一样的人，你们互相点头，越点越极端。
en: Algorithms amplify this instinct ten thousand times, plus the 'echo chamber effect': everyone around you is like you, nodding at each other, nodding ever more extremely.

text: 最后你不是在思考，你是在被喂养。
en: In the end, you are not thinking; you are being fed.

text: 怎么破？
en: How to break it?

text: 给你五个极其落地的操作。
en: Here are five extremely practical operations.

text: 第一、主动关注三个你讨厌但理性的人
en: First: proactively follow three people you dislike but who are rational.

text: 不是让你认同他们，是让你知道他们怎么想。
en: Not to make you agree with them, but to let you know how they think.

text: 每次刷到他们的内容，别急着划走，问一句：“他为什么这么想？
en: Every time you scroll to their content, don't rush to swipe away; ask: 'Why does he think this way?

text: 他的证据是什么？
en: What is his evidence?

text: ”这叫“认知多样性疫苗”。
en: ' This is called a 'cognitive diversity vaccine'.

text: 第二、每周做一次“信息断食”
en: Second: do an 'information fast' once a week.

text: 选半天，关掉所有推送，去线下和人面对面聊天。
en: Pick half a day, turn off all pushes, and go chat face-to-face with people offline.

text: 去菜市场听大妈骂菜价，去公园听大爷吹牛。
en: Go to the wet market and listen to aunties cursing vegetable prices; go to the park and listen to uncles bragging.

text: 真实世界的噪音，比算法的精准更接近真相。
en: The noise of the real world is closer to truth than the precision of algorithms.

text: 第三、对任何信息问三个问题
en: Third: ask three questions about any piece of information.

text: 谁说的？
en: Who said it?

text: 他有什么利益？
en: What interests does he have?

text: 反方怎么说？
en: What does the other side say?

text: 别急着转发，先查原始信源。
en: Don't rush to forward it; first check the original source.

text: 你转发的每一条谣言，都是在给别人的镰刀递韭菜。
en: Every rumour you forward is handing leeks to someone else's sickle.

text: 第四、建立“反脆弱信息食谱”
en: Fourth: build an 'antifragile information diet'.

text: 30%你认同的，30%你反对的，30%你完全陌生的。
en: 30% what you agree with, 30% what you oppose, 30% completely unfamiliar to you.

text: 强制自己每个月读一本你以前绝不会碰的书，关注一个你完全不懂的领域。
en: Force yourself to read one book every month that you would never have touched before, and follow a field you completely don't understand.

text: 你的大脑需要异见，就像身体需要维生素。
en: Your brain needs dissent, just as the body needs vitamins.

text: 第五、每月做一次“观点拆迁”
en: Fifth: do a 'view demolition' once a month.

text: 写一篇你反对的观点，用最强论据，写到你自己都快被说服。
en: Write an article for a view you oppose, using the strongest arguments, until you almost convince yourself.

text: 这个动作，比读一百篇鸡汤更能拆掉你思维里的墙。
en: This action dismantles the walls in your thinking better than reading a hundred chicken-soup articles.

text: 信息茧房最可怕的地方，不是你不知道世界，而是你以为你知道。
en: The most terrifying aspect of information cocoons is not that you don't know the world, but that you think you know it.

text: 别让算法替你思考，别让舒适区成为你的坟墓，你的大脑，不是别人的跑马场。
en: Don't let algorithms think for you; don't let your comfort zone become your grave. Your brain is not someone else's racetrack.

text: 最简单的方法就是学习逻辑。
en: The simplest method is to learn logic.

text: 逻辑可以让你拥有预测功能，错误的信息很容易被识破，当然这样需要你有基本的正确信息，即底层逻辑，但是，大部分人的底层逻辑都是错的。
en: Logic gives you predictive ability; wrong information is easily seen through. Of course, this requires you to have basically correct information, i.e., underlying logic. However, most people's underlying logic is wrong.

text: 其实大多数人是被洗脑造成的底层逻辑错误，要想恢复自然的科学的逻辑实际上是非常困难的，这需要你有主动摆脱错误的底层逻辑的观念，自然也不是什么难事。
en: In fact, most people have wrong underlying logic caused by brainwashing. To restore natural, scientific logic is actually very difficult, requiring you to have the concept of proactively getting rid of wrong underlying logic — but naturally, it is not that difficult either.

text: 在知乎看到这样的提问，不免感到错愕。
en: Seeing such a question on Zhihu, I can't help feeling surprised.

text: 知乎的左中右派网友俱全。
en: Zhihu has netizens from the left, centre and right all present.

text: 各种观念激烈碰撞，信源丰富。
en: All kinds of views collide fiercely, with rich sources.

text: 只要注重独立思考，常来知乎了解时政，就可以脱离信息茧房。
en: As long as you focus on independent thinking and often come to Zhihu to learn about current affairs, you can escape information cocoons.

text: 当然这仅对独立思考的人有效。
en: Of course, this only works for people who think independently.

text: 如果某人缺乏独立思考的习惯，那么他永远无法脱离信息茧房。
en: If someone lacks the habit of independent thinking, he can never escape information cocoons.

text: 因为他的大脑已经被自我囚禁，他的大脑就是他的信息茧房。
en: Because his brain has already imprisoned itself; his brain is his information cocoon.

text: 就算他处在完全开放的信息时空也无济于事。
en: Even if he is in a completely open information space-time, it will not help.

text: 首先是不能听一面之词，要看多方的信息。
en: First, you cannot listen to only one side; you must look at information from multiple sides.

text: 其次是要符合逻辑，有些东西看着就不符合逻辑，那肯定有鬼。
en: Second, it must conform to logic. Some things look illogical at a glance — there must be something fishy.

text: 哪怕是同一个事儿，事实骨架差不多，但包的“意义外衣”一换，味道就完全相反了。
en: Even for the same matter, with roughly the same factual skeleton, once the 'cloak of meaning' wrapped around it changes, the flavour becomes completely opposite.

text: 但是事情还是那个事儿，意思和理解就南辕北辙了。
en: But the matter is still that matter; the meaning and understanding become diametrically opposed.

text: 我举个例子：
en: Let me give an example:

text: 美国主流叙事：日本帝国主义卑鄙无耻的偷袭、不宣而战、背信弃义的“国耻日”，把美国彻底拖入正义的反法西斯战争。
en: Mainstream American narrative: Japan's despicable, shameless surprise attack, undeclared war, treacherous 'Day of National Humiliation', dragging America completely into the just anti-fascist war.

text: 日本右翼/部分军国主义叙事视角：绝望中被迫的自卫反击战，美国通过石油禁运等早已把日本逼到绝境，珍珠港是“破釜沉舟”的最后一搏，是“哀兵”之举。
en: Japanese right-wing / partial militarist narrative perspective: a desperate self-defensive counterattack, with America having already driven Japan to a dead end through oil embargoes and the like; Pearl Harbor was a 'burning one's boats' last gamble, an act of a 'grieving army'.

text: 从“无耻偷袭”到“被迫殊死一搏”，动机与道德评价完全颠倒。
en: From 'shameless surprise attack' to 'forced fight to the death', motives and moral evaluations are completely reversed.

text: 然后洗的那些昭和青年群情激愤，上赶着玉碎。
en: Then those brainwashed Showa youths were filled with righteous indignation, rushing to die honourably.

text: 甚至同一个事情，同一个立场，因为春秋笔法也能意义和意思南辕北辙。
en: Even for the same matter and the same stance, Spring and Autumn Annals-style wording can make meaning and sense diametrically opposed.

text: 总之还是那句话：带点脑子
en: In short, still that saying: use your brain a bit.

text: 下班回到家，累得连饭都不想吃，往沙发上一瘫，手指开始下意识地往下滑。
en: After work, returning home, so tired you don't even want to eat, collapsing onto the sofa, fingers starting to slide subconsciously.

text: 一个视频接一个视频，一条段子接一条段子。
en: One video after another, one joke after another.

text: 你也知道这些东西没什么营养，但就是停不下来。
en: You know these things have no nutrition, but you just can't stop.

text: 你有没有过这种经历？
en: Have you had this experience?

text: 等你回过神来，已经凌晨一点了。
en: When you come to your senses, it is already 1 am.

text: 你感到一阵巨大的空虚，然后开始自责。
en: You feel a huge emptiness, then start blaming yourself.

text: 我怎么这么不自律？
en: 'Why am I so undisciplined?

text: 又浪费了一晚上。
en: Wasted another evening.'

text: 先停一下。
en: Stop for a moment.

text: 今天我想替你说句实话，这不怪你。
en: Today I want to speak a truth for you: this is not your fault.

text: 但有一件事，比怪你更让人不舒服。
en: But there is something more uncomfortable than blaming you.

text: 不是你的意志力出了问题，是你掉进了一个经过精密设计的心理圈套里。
en: It is not your willpower that has a problem; you have fallen into a precisely designed psychological trap.

text: 而这个圈套，恰恰是利用了你最脆弱的时候。
en: And this trap precisely exploits your most vulnerable moments.

text: 最先困住人的，是心力被一点点耗干。
en: What traps people first is mental energy being drained bit by bit.

text: 你白天在单位，要忍受老板的脾气，要处理同事的推诿，要应付无穷无尽的琐事。
en: During the day at work, you must endure your boss's temper, handle colleagues' buck-passing, and deal with endless trivial matters.

text: 这一天下来，你的大脑已经累了，只会挑不用动脑的东西看。
en: After a day like this, your brain is already tired and only picks things that require no thinking.

text: 它不是懒，是自动进入了省电模式。
en: It is not laziness; it automatically enters power-saving mode.

text: 心力被榨干是什么感觉？
en: What does it feel like to have your mental energy drained?

text: 就是你知道刷手机没意义，但你就是控制不住。
en: It is knowing that scrolling your phone is meaningless, but you just cannot control yourself.

text: 你知道早睡对身体好，但你就是不想动。
en: You know going to bed early is good for your health, but you just don't want to move.

text: 不是不想改变。
en: It is not that you don't want to change.

text: 是真没力气了。
en: It is that you really have no energy left.

text: 这时候，短视频、爽文、情绪骂战刚好凑过来。
en: At this time, short videos, feel-good articles and emotional flame wars happen to come over.

text: 它们不需要你费劲，就能给你一种我好像学到了什么、我好像参与了什么的错觉。
en: They don't require you to exert effort, yet give you an illusion that 'I seem to have learned something, I seem to have participated in something'.

text: 我年轻那会儿在车间干活，干完活回宿舍就是累。
en: When I was young working in a workshop, after work I returned to the dormitory exhausted.

text: 一身汗都没擦，就会先刷几条没营养的网文。
en: Without even wiping off my sweat, I would first scroll a few nutrition-free web articles.

text: 那时候还没有算法这回事，就是觉得脑子已经转不动了，得看点不用动脑子的东西。
en: At that time there was no such thing as algorithms; I just felt my brain could no longer turn, and needed to watch something that required no thinking.

text: 后来我才琢磨明白，那种不用动脑子的感觉，才是最贵的。
en: Later I figured out that the feeling of not needing to think is the most expensive.

text: 你以为你是在放松，其实只是被动接受投喂。
en: You think you are relaxing, but in fact you are just passively accepting feeding.

text: 而且平台利用完你之后，还会让你觉得是自己不行。
en: And after platforms use you up, they make you feel it is your own fault.

text: 它拿走了你的注意力，再让你为管不住自己内疚一遍。
en: They take your attention, then make you feel guilty again for not controlling yourself.

text: 你在它眼里，就是一块还能用的电池。
en: In their eyes, you are just a battery that can still be used.

text: 有人会说，既然被动不行，我主动去搜总行了吧？
en: Someone might say: since passivity doesn't work, actively searching should work, right?

text: 你试过主动搜相反观点吧？
en: Have you tried actively searching for opposing views?

text: 没用。
en: Useless.

text: 不是因为你搜得不够努力，是因为你搜东西用的工具、搜到的范围、用来判断什么是相反的标准，全都是这个系统给你的。
en: Not because you didn't search hard enough, but because the tools you use to search, the scope of what you find, and the standards you use to judge what counts as opposite are all given to you by this system.

text: 你以为你在四处漫游，其实只是走在预设好的草径上。
en: You think you are roaming everywhere, but in fact you are only walking on preset grass paths.

text: 路边长的全是你爱吃的草，吃得自在，却始终跨不出划定的地界。
en: All growing by the roadside is grass you love to eat. You eat comfortably, but never step beyond the demarcated boundary.

text: 我有个朋友，不知道从哪听来的，说要戒算法。
en: I have a friend who, hearing from somewhere that one should quit algorithms,

text: 把常用的平台卸了，下了个冷门的。
en: uninstalled commonly used platforms and downloaded an obscure one.

text: 折腾仨月，有天跑来跟我说：那边更狠，连骂算法的帖子都往我脸上推。
en: After three months of fussing, one day he came to me and said: that side is even worse — even posts cursing algorithms are pushed in my face.

text: 他以为他翻出去了。
en: He thought he had climbed out.

text: 其实他只是翻进了另一面镜子。
en: In fact, he had only climbed into another mirror.

text: 草径还是那条草径，只是换了个方向长。
en: The grass path is still that grass path, only growing in a different direction.

text: 它不光要你待在里面，它还要你觉得自己在往外走。
en: It not only wants you to stay inside; it also wants you to feel you are walking out.

text: 因为往外走这个动作，比待着不动产生的数据更多。
en: Because the act of walking out generates more data than staying still.

text: 说到这儿，我突然想起小时候见过的一只山雀。
en: Speaking of this, I suddenly remember a titmouse I saw as a child.

text: 有人把鸟笼靠墙放着，那山雀天天扑腾着去够墙上的一小块光斑。
en: Someone placed a birdcage against a wall, and the titmouse fluttered every day trying to reach a small patch of light on the wall.

text: 旁人以为它渴望外面的天地，好心把笼子挪到院子，眼前整片山野都敞开了。
en: Others thought it longed for the outside world, and kindly moved the cage to the yard, where the whole mountain wilderness opened before its eyes.

text: 可山雀反而慌了，乱飞了一阵，最后缩回角落，继续盯着那一小片阳光。
en: But the titmouse panicked instead, flew around wildly, and finally shrank back into a corner, continuing to stare at that small patch of sunlight.

text: 它或许根本不是向往广阔的天地，只是贪恋那一点不用费力就能抓到手的光亮。
en: Perhaps it never longed for the vast world; it just coveted that bit of light it could grasp without effort.

text: 真把自由摆在面前，它反倒不敢接了。
en: When freedom was truly placed before it, it dared not accept it.

text: 我们嘴上说着想跳出茧房，实际上贪恋的，也不过是算法随手递过来的那点廉价安慰。
en: We say we want to jump out of cocoons, but in fact what we covet is just the cheap comfort algorithms casually hand over.

text: 不是没有别的信息，是舍不得放下那份不用动脑子的轻松。
en: It is not that there is no other information; it is that we cannot bear to put down that effortless ease.

text: 更狠的是，你以为你至少还保留了一样东西，你的愤怒。
en: Even worse: you think you at least retain one thing — your anger.

text: 可你仔细想想，连这个，也早就被算计进去了。
en: But think carefully: even this was calculated long ago.

text: 还有一件藏得更深的事，放到后面慢慢说。
en: There is something hidden even deeper; I'll tell it slowly later.

text: 你白天被老板骂了，心里憋着一团火。
en: During the day, your boss scolded you, and you held a ball of fire in your heart.

text: 晚上你刷手机，刚好刷到一条吐槽老板、宣泄委屈的段子。
en: At night, you scroll your phone and happen to scroll to a joke venting about bosses and grievances.

text: 你看完笑了一下，觉得解气了，顺手点了个赞，转发到群里。
en: After watching, you laughed, felt relieved, casually liked it, and forwarded it to a group.

text: 你想过没有，那个解气的一下，恰恰把你原本可以用来干正事的劲给卸了。
en: Have you thought about it? That moment of relief precisely discharged the energy you could have used for proper business.

text: 你本来可以拿那团火去投简历、去学个新东西、去跟你老板把话说清楚。
en: You could have used that fire to send résumés, learn something new, or talk things through with your boss.

text: 但你把它吐在一个段子里了。
en: But you vented it in a joke.

text: 那团火没烧向该烧的地方，烧完你就累了，睡了，第二天照常上班。
en: That fire did not burn where it should have; after burning, you were tired, slept, and went to work as usual the next day.

text: 你那团火，最后结算进它的流量报表里。
en: Your fire was finally settled into its traffic report.

text: 你骂完之后那点痛快，就是它这个月发出去的奖金。
en: That bit of pleasure after you cursed is the bonus it handed out this month.

text: 你在它的账本上，就是一串数字。
en: On its ledger, you are just a string of numbers.

text: 可你自己过的日子，不只是一串数字。
en: But the life you live is not just a string of numbers.

text: 它未必不让你看见真相，却会慢慢让你懒得去戳破真相。
en: It may not stop you from seeing the truth, but it will slowly make you too lazy to puncture the truth.

text: 你可能会想，那我至少还可以恨它。
en: You might think: at least I can still hate it.

text: 别急着恨。
en: Don't rush to hate.

text: 恨，也是它留的一个按钮。
en: Hate is also a button it left for you.

text: 你越恨，停留时长越长，它越开心。
en: The more you hate, the longer you stay, the happier it is.

text: 你不信？
en: Don't believe me?

text: 再想想。
en: Think again.

text: 你骂完它之后，是不是觉得痛快了一点？
en: After cursing it, do you feel a bit relieved?

text: 那点痛快，就是你给它的续费。
en: That bit of relief is the renewal fee you paid it.

text: 而且最邪门的是，你越骂它，它越活。
en: And the strangest thing is: the more you curse it, the more alive it becomes.

text: 你每一条愤怒的评论、每一次转发骂它的帖子，后台都记着：用户活跃度加一。
en: Every angry comment you make, every forwarded post cursing it, is recorded in the backend: user activity +1.

text: 你以为你在反抗，你其实在给它续命。
en: You think you are resisting, but in fact you are renewing its life.

text: 愤怒本身可以促人觉醒，有它的社会价值。
en: Anger itself can awaken people and has its social value.

text: 但从流量机制上看，仅仅是在为这一条内容增加热度，不等于你的批判本身毫无意义。
en: But from the traffic mechanism's perspective, it merely adds heat to this piece of content; this does not mean your criticism itself is meaningless.

text: 它没打算害你。
en: It did not intend to harm you.

text: 从你下载那天起，每一步都是算过的，它只是转起来就停不住。
en: From the day you downloaded it, every step was calculated; it just keeps spinning and cannot stop.

text: 这不是偶然出的漏洞，是它自诞生起就写好的逻辑。
en: This is not an accidental loophole; it is logic written since its birth.

text: 那怎么办？
en: So what to do?

text: 网上不少高赞回答，教人主动搜相反观点、少点赞少评论去规避算法。
en: Many highly praised answers online teach people to actively search for opposing views, like and comment less to avoid algorithms.

text: 这些办法不能说错，但往往漏掉一个前提：人得先有余力，才能谈选择。
en: These methods cannot be said to be wrong, but they often miss a premise: a person must first have spare energy before talking about choices.

text: 你去问一个刚下流水线的姑娘，她晚上刷不刷短视频。
en: Ask a girl who just got off the assembly line whether she scrolls short videos at night.

text: 她肯定刷。
en: She definitely does.

text: 你让她交叉验证？
en: You ask her to cross-verify?

text: 她连澡都不想洗。
en: She doesn't even want to take a shower.

text: 或者你哪天点外卖注意看一眼，骑手等红灯那几十秒，十有八九在刷手机。
en: Or one day when you order takeaway, look: in the tens of seconds a delivery rider waits at a red light, nine times out of ten he is scrolling his phone.

text: 那是他一天里唯一不疼的片刻。
en: That is the only painless moment in his day.

text: 你跟他说拓宽信源？
en: You tell him to broaden his sources?

text: 你让一个连喘息缝隙都没有的人靠意志力去打破一堵墙，不是励志，是站着说话不腰疼。
en: Asking a person who doesn't even have a breathing gap to break down a wall by willpower is not inspirational; it is talking without feeling the pain.

text: 你能看见什么样的信息，往往不全是好奇心说了算，更多取决于你的工时、收入，还有一天下来还剩下多少精力这些实打实的现实。
en: What kind of information you can see often depends not entirely on curiosity, but more on solid realities like your working hours, income, and how much energy you have left after a day.

text: 所以，别再拿自律来PUA自己了。
en: So stop using self-discipline to PUA yourself.

text: 你需要的不是鸡汤，是清醒。
en: What you need is not chicken soup, but clarity.

text: 说到这儿，我自己都觉得有点啰嗦了。
en: Speaking of this, I feel I am being a bit long-winded.

text: 其实这些事你们心里比谁都明白，我就是忍不住多说两句。
en: Actually, you all understand these things better than anyone; I just can't help saying a few more words.

text: 说到底就三件事。
en: In the end, it comes down to three things.

text: 你一件一件听。
en: Listen to them one by one.

text: 第一件，累了只想刷短视频，真不是你懒，是身子骨扛不住了。
en: First: being tired and only wanting to scroll short videos is really not laziness; your body can't take it anymore.

text: 先别骂自己，允许自己糊里糊涂歇一会儿。
en: Don't scold yourself first; allow yourself to rest in a daze for a while.

text: 我年轻时候抢修完也那样，没见谁因为多刷了两天手机就完了。
en: When I was young, after emergency repairs, I was like that too. I never saw anyone ruined just because they scrolled their phone for two extra days.

text: 第二件，歇够了之后，人还是会拿起手机。
en: Second: after resting enough, people will still pick up their phones.

text: 这不是你的错。
en: This is not your fault.

text: 这是身体记住的路径。
en: This is a path the body remembers.

text: 真正要改的，不是意志力，是这条路径。
en: What truly needs changing is not willpower, but this path.

text: 这条路径里，最隐蔽的一段，就是那些让你哭着转发的情绪内容。
en: In this path, the most hidden section is those emotional contents that make you cry and forward.

text: 有一部分，是在替你消化本该变成行动的能量。
en: A part of them is digesting for you the energy that should have become action.

text: 适度宣泄本身无可厚非，但存在一种很常见的心理现象：
en: Moderate venting is itself blameless, but there is a very common psychological phenomenon:

text: 对一部分人来说，如果仅仅停留在情绪解气，没有落到现实行动，情绪压力被提前释放之后，就很难再生发出改变现状的冲动。
en: For some people, if they only stop at emotional relief without landing on real action, after emotional pressure is released early, it becomes hard to regenerate the impulse to change the status quo.

text: 下次再被戳中时，停一秒问自己：这份共鸣，是不是把该做的事儿给抵消了？
en: Next time you are struck, pause for a second and ask yourself: is this resonance cancelling out something I should be doing?

text: 第三件，很多你以为属于自己的偏好，其实是别人替你筛好的。
en: Third: many preferences you think are your own are actually screened for you by others.

text: 这不是你的错。
en: This is not your fault.

text: 看清这层窗户纸，就不用再对着它夸屋里空气好了。
en: Seeing through this layer of window paper, you no longer need to praise the air in the room facing it.

text: 这三件事你记不住也没事。
en: It doesn't matter if you can't remember these three things.

text: 你就记住一句：别把困住你的东西，当成你自己的选择。
en: Just remember one sentence: don't treat what traps you as your own choice.

text: 说到这儿，你肯定想说：叔，我懂了，明天开始我就少刷。
en: Speaking of this, you must want to say: Uncle, I understand; starting tomorrow I'll scroll less.

text: 别。
en: Don't.

text: 你明天刻意少刷的那半小时，未必是你获得自由，很多时候只是出于内疚。
en: The half hour you deliberately scroll less tomorrow may not be freedom you gain; often it is just guilt.

text: 内疚驱动的自律撑不过三天，紧绷过后反弹，你反而会更加责怪自己。
en: Guilt-driven self-discipline won't last three days; after tightening, it rebounds, and you will blame yourself even more.

text: 所以别急着改。
en: So don't rush to change.

text: 先把这个看清楚。
en: First see this clearly.

text: 然后呢？
en: Then?

text: 然后如果你有余力，不是逼自己，是你哪天真的歇过来了，喘上气了，你可以想想更大的事。
en: Then, if you have spare energy — not forcing yourself, but when you truly recover one day and catch your breath — you can think about bigger things.

text: 这些平台该归谁管？
en: Who should regulate these platforms?

text: 算法对谁透明？
en: To whom are algorithms transparent?

text: 还有你的注意力，凭什么变成别人的利润？
en: And your attention — why does it become someone else's profit?

text: 这些不是单靠某一个人就能解决的问题，需要更多人看见、更多人去讨论，推动规则变得更合理。
en: These are not problems any single person can solve alone; they require more people to see, more people to discuss, and to push rules to become more reasonable.

text: 一个人看清了，是清醒。
en: One person seeing clearly is clarity.

text: 一群人看清了，才是改变的开始。
en: A group of people seeing clearly is the beginning of change.

text: 但第一步，是别再把困住你的东西，当成你自己的选择了。
en: But the first step is to stop treating what traps you as your own choice.

text: 看清这件事的那天，茧房就已经裂了一条缝。
en: The day you see this clearly, the cocoon has already cracked a seam.

text: 这条缝不会让你一夜之间跳出系统，但至少能让你在下次刷到一条特别解气的内容时，试一次：
en: This seam won't let you jump out of the system overnight, but at least it lets you, next time you scroll to a particularly relieving piece of content, try once:

text: 看完，别点。
en: After reading, don't click.

text: 就那么划过去。
en: Just swipe past.

text: 不是因为你自律，是因为那一下没点，是今天唯一一个它没预测到的动作。
en: Not because you are disciplined, but because that one non-click is the only action it didn't predict today.

text: 说到底困住我们的，往往不是一堵密不透风的高墙，而是那一份无需反思、唾手可得的廉价情绪安慰。
en: In the end, what traps us is often not an airtight high wall, but that cheap emotional comfort requiring no reflection and within easy reach.

text: 脚边的猫翻了个身，呼噜声没断。
en: The cat at my feet turned over, its purring uninterrupted.

text: 它不懂什么茧房，只知道这会儿暖和。
en: It doesn't understand cocoons; it only knows it is warm right now.

text: 窗外的路灯还亮着。
en: The streetlights outside the window are still on.

text: 我伸手去把台灯拨到夜档。
en: I reach out to turn the desk lamp to night mode.

text: 拨完我才想起来，这开关我上个月也拨过一回。
en: After turning it, I remember I also turned this switch last month.

text: 那回灯亮了三秒又暗了。
en: That time the light stayed on for three seconds and then went dark.

text: 这次不知道能亮多久。
en: This time, I don't know how long it will stay on.

text: 手还是伸了。
en: My hand still reached out.

text: 不是因为我逼自己，是因为灯在那儿。
en: Not because I forced myself, but because the lamp is there.
